monthly_review.summary: This month shows increased aerobic stimulus and improved pacing consistency, but with a notable drop in cadence and efficiency compared to last month. The shift toward higher-intensity zone distribution reflects intentional training progression.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence dropped 9 spm month-over-month — the largest absolute change among all metrics and a potential contributor to reduced running economy on faster efforts.

goal_tracker.message: You need 0.5 more km across up to 5 remaining sessions — easily achievable with one additional 1.0 km easy run or by adding 500 m to any upcoming session.

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite slower avg pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.28 to 13.35 m/sec per bpm, indicating better oxygen utilization per heartbeat — likely supported by the 23% Z1 time this month (vs only 4% last month), suggesting enhanced recovery capacity and foundational aerobic development.

insights.title: Significant shift toward higher-intensity zones
insights.body: Z3–Z4 time increased from 48% (36% Z3 + 12% Z4) last month to 43% (26% Z3 + 17% Z4) this month, while Z1 nearly quadrupled (4% → 23%). This reflects a more polarized approach — beneficial for endurance gains — but Z5 remains low (5%) and unchanged from prior trend.

insights.title: Cadence decline correlates with pace variability and vertical oscillation increase
insights.body: Avg cadence fell from 150 to 141 spm; notably, the two fastest recent runs (4/12 and 4/22) had cadences of 146 and 150 spm, while the slowest (4/26, 14:00/km) dropped to 87 spm — and vertical oscillation rose to 8.8 cm on 4/22 (vs 6.4–7.8 cm elsewhere), suggesting form breakdown at fatigue or under mixed-intensity demands.

insights.title: Aerobic TE increased without HR elevation, signaling improved load tolerance
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE rose +0.2 (3.0 → 3.2) while avg HR held steady at 142–143 bpm — indicating the same heart rate is now generating greater physiological stimulus, consistent with VO2 max rising from 34.0 to 35.0 across recent runs.

recommendations.action: Perform a 4 km Zone 2 run (HR 125–135 bpm) with cadence consciously held ≥148 spm using metronome or audio cue — focus on light, quick steps and minimal vertical bounce.
recommendations.reason: Your cadence dropped 9 spm MoM and your slowest-effort run (4/26) fell to 87 spm, revealing neuromuscular drift; rebuilding rhythm in Z2 reinforces efficient stride mechanics without fatigue interference.

recommendations.action: Replace one midweek run with a 20-min progressive tempo: start at Z2 (135 bpm), build to Z3 (150–155 bpm) for final 8 min, holding cadence ≥145 spm throughout.
recommendations.reason: Your Z3 time increased but your best pace (428 sec/km = 7:08/km) occurred at 163 bpm (4/12) — aligning pace and HR intent will improve lactate buffering and race-specific efficiency.

recommendations.action: Add 2 × 30-sec strides (95% effort, relaxed form) post-warmup on your next two easy runs, focusing on silent footstrike and vertical oscillation <7.5 cm.
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time decreased (311 → 298 ms) on faster runs but vertical oscillation spiked to 8.8 cm on 4/22 — strides reinforce elastic recoil and reduce braking forces without adding volume.

weekly_focus.description: Reinforce neuromuscular coordination at varied intensities while protecting aerobic foundation — prioritize cadence consistency, controlled vertical oscillation, and intentional HR-zone adherence.
